## Why this unit matters

- The observation models chapter produced case reports from a **known** process.
- Now reverse the arrow: given only the reports, what are the parameters?
- The **frequentist** view: parameters are fixed unknowns; uncertainty is the
  sampling behaviour of estimators.

::: {.notes}
This deck runs in the isolated environment `environments/ch10`, pinned via the
document's `julia.exeflags`, which carries mutually compatible
`ProfileLikelihood`, `Optimization`, and `OrdinaryDiffEq` versions.
:::

## Model and likelihood

Deterministic SIR ODE + Poisson observations, estimating
$\theta=(i_0,\beta)$ with $c=10,\gamma=0.25$ fixed. Model incidence
$x_t(\theta)$ gives the Poisson log-likelihood

$$
\ell(\theta)=\sum_{t=1}^{n}\big[y_t\log x_t(\theta)-x_t(\theta)-\log(y_t!)\big].
$$

Profile out nuisance parameters and use Wilks' theorem for intervals:

$$
\ell_p(\beta)=\max_{i_0}\ell(i_0,\beta),\qquad
\text{95\% CI}:\ \ell_p(\beta)\ge\ell(\hat\theta)-1.92.
$$

::: {.notes}
The threshold $1.92=\tfrac12\chi^2_{1,0.95}$ is the Venzon–Moolgavkar
construction implemented by `ProfileLikelihood.jl`.
:::

## Fitting: MLE and profile intervals

```{julia}
#| label: ch08-fit
#| output: false
using OrdinaryDiffEq, ProfileLikelihood, Optimization, OptimizationOptimJL
using Distributions, StableRNGs, DataFrames

function sir_ode08!(du, u, p, t)
    S, I, R, C = u
    β, c, γ = p
    N = S + I + R
    infection = β * c * I / N * S
    du[1] = -infection
    du[2] = infection - γ * I
    du[3] = γ * I
    du[4] = infection
end

δt, tmax = 1.0, 40.0
u0 = [990.0, 10.0, 0.0, 0.0]
p = [0.05, 10.0, 0.25]
prob08 = ODEProblem(sir_ode08!, u0, (0.0, tmax), p)
sol = solve(prob08, Tsit5(); saveat = δt)
incidence = Array(sol)[4, 2:end] .- Array(sol)[4, 1:(end - 1)]
data = rand.(StableRNG(20240607), Poisson.(incidence))

function loglik(θ, data, integrator)
    i₀, β = θ
    integrator.p[1] = β; integrator.p[2] = 10.0; integrator.p[3] = 0.25
    I = i₀ * 1000.0
    reinit!(integrator, [1000.0 - I, I, 0.0, 0.0])
    solve!(integrator)
    C = Array(integrator.sol)[4, :]
    X = C[2:end] .- C[1:(end - 1)]
    any(X .<= 0) && return -Inf
    sum(logpdf.(Poisson.(X), data))
end

prob = LikelihoodProblem(loglik, [0.01, 0.1], sir_ode08!, u0, (0.0, tmax);
    syms = [:i₀, :β], data = data, ode_parameters = p,
    ode_kwargs = (verbose = false, saveat = δt),
    f_kwargs = (adtype = Optimization.AutoFiniteDiff(),),
    prob_kwargs = (lb = [0.0, 0.0], ub = [1.0, 1.0]), ode_alg = Tsit5())

mle_sol = mle(prob, NelderMead())
θ̂ = get_mle(mle_sol)
prof = profile(prob, mle_sol; alg = NelderMead(), parallel = false)
ci = get_confidence_intervals(prof)
```

```{julia}
#| label: ch08-results
DataFrame(parameter = ["i₀", "β"], truth = [0.01, 0.05], mle = round.(θ̂; digits = 4),
    ci_lower = [round(ci[i][1]; digits = 4) for i in 1:2],
    ci_upper = [round(ci[i][2]; digits = 4) for i in 1:2])
```

::: {.notes}
The MLE recovers the generating parameters and both 95% profile intervals cover
the truth. Sample counts and grid are small so the deck runs quickly; a real
profile would use a finer grid.
:::

## Profile log-likelihoods

```{julia}
#| label: fig-slide-ch08-profile
#| fig-cap: "Profile log-likelihoods for i₀ and β. Dashed line: 95% threshold; blue dotted: interval endpoints; red: truth."
using CairoMakie
CairoMakie.activate!(type = "png")
threshold = -0.5 * quantile(Chisq(1), 0.95)
truth = [0.01, 0.05]; names = ["i₀", "β"]
fig08 = Figure(size = (900, 360))
for i in 1:2
    ax = Axis(fig08[1, i]; xlabel = names[i], ylabel = "profile log-likelihood")
    lines!(ax, get_parameter_values(prof, i), get_profile_values(prof, i);
        color = :steelblue, linewidth = 3)
    hlines!(ax, [threshold]; color = :black, linestyle = :dash)
    vlines!(ax, [truth[i]]; color = :firebrick, linewidth = 2)
    vlines!(ax, [ci[i][1], ci[i][2]]; color = :steelblue, linestyle = :dot)
    ylims!(ax, threshold - 1.5, 0.4)
end
fig08
```

::: {.notes}
Each curve is normalised to zero at the MLE; the interval is where it lies above
the dashed Wilks threshold. A flat profile would signal weak identifiability.
:::

## Takeaways and limitations

- MLE via `Optimization.jl`; profile CIs via `ProfileLikelihood.jl`.
- Nelder–Mead is **local** — use multistart before trusting one fit.
- The $\chi^2$ calibration is **asymptotic**; small samples may mis-cover.
- $\beta$ and $c$ enter only as $\beta c$ $\Rightarrow$ not separately
  identifiable (the sensitivity and identifiability chapter).
- Intervals summarise sampling variability, not prior knowledge — the Bayesian inference chapter is
  the Bayesian counterpart.

Read the [book chapter](../../chapters/10-parameter-estimation.html); see
[Optimization.jl](https://docs.sciml.ai/Optimization/stable/) and
[ProfileLikelihood.jl](https://github.com/DanielVandH/ProfileLikelihood.jl).

::: {.notes}
Emphasise that "narrow interval" is a statement about this data-generating setup,
not a guarantee that every biological parameter is learnable.
:::
